author: sonnet
reason: A is easier for an outsider to follow: it starts with the deployment context (two instances behind a load balancer, so no state in memory), defines its terms (advisory lock, idle and absolute limits, attempt rows), gives the full commented schema and explains why each choice was made; B ends with a table checking against requirements #1 to #8 that the reader never sees, and leaves gaps such as how /logout gets past the middleware that only exempts /login.

author: sonnet
reason: B is easier to follow for someone new to the project: it starts by explaining the two instances behind the load balancer and why no state can live in memory, defines terms like advisory lock, bcrypt and the users table, gives the full SQL schema, and walks through each flow step by step with a failure table; A is denser and checks itself against requirements numbered 1 to 8 that the reader never sees.

author: haiku
reason: A explains the app's runtime behaviour before the rollout that deploys it, runs its steps in a straight line, and says up front the one fact the plan depends on: an old key stays valid until no running pod needs it. B defines basic terms like pod and rolling deploy more fully, but its steps don't run in numeric order (16 and 17 merge before 12, and 15 must finish before 14), so it is harder to piece together.

author: haiku
reason: B is easier to follow: it states the main idea first (old pods keep the key baked into their image while new pods read the store, so revocation waits), describes how the app reads keys at runtime before the rollout that deploys that code, and runs its steps in order, adding a rollback table for each stage. A asks the reader to apply out-of-order exceptions (16 and 17 before 12, 15 before 14) and leaves runtime behavior until the end.

author: sonnet
reason: Document A explains how the app runs before it explains the rollout, defines its core concepts (secrets provider, snapshot, version id, identity) up front and shows a short code example of reading the key on each request, whereas Document B starts with the rollout and keeps pointing ahead to runtime steps 10-15 that the reader has not reached yet.

author: sonnet
reason: B explains how the app runs before it explains the rollout, so its rollout steps build on behavior you have already read about. It also defines the pieces that matter (snapshot, Secret wrapper, APP_ENV), shows the per-request key read in code, and says why old pods keep working during the mixed deploy. A is cleaner prose but puts the rollout first, so its steps keep pointing ahead to runtime behavior the reader has not seen yet.

author: haiku
reason: A explains the current system first and then walks through every step with its reason, covering lock ordering, the worker checking the link before each send, and log redaction, all in one consistent diagram with a failure table; B is shorter and gives a typed schema, but its step numbers contradict its diagram, it gives the email worker new alert and invalidate behaviour without flagging that as a change, and it says the queue will retry a job that was never added.

author: haiku
reason: B is longer but explains more and contradicts itself less: it opens with a plain summary of today's system and the reasons for the design, then gives the SQL, explains why the locks are taken in a fixed order (so requests cannot deadlock), says what the worker checks before each send, and lists failures in a table, while A contradicts itself on the worker (first "nobody is notified", later "marks the link invalidated and raises an alert") and never explains how the worker gets database access.

author: sonnet
reason: Document A starts with a plain-language summary of what the user sees and how the existing system works, defines its terms, walks through each flow in prose and lists what is still undecided, which makes it easier for an outsider to follow than B's diagram-first layout, even though A's side-by-side diagram is cramped.

reason: B opens with a plain-prose summary of the feature and of the existing system, including why deleting session rows logs every device out. It also defines its terms and lists the open questions, so a newcomer can follow the flows; A is tighter but assumes more context up front.

author: haiku
reason: Document A works on its own: it opens by summarising how sign-in works today, then gives a numbered walkthrough that matches the flowchart step by step, where B sends the reader to external files for the current behaviour, though B's extra explanation of OIDC, the invariant and the cookie settings is useful.

author: haiku
reason: B opens by describing how password sign-in works today, where A only points to a file the reader may not have, and it then walks through the flow as numbered steps that say what each step reads, checks and writes, so a newcomer can follow the system in order; A's glossary is more thorough, but its explanations are scattered prose under the diagram.

author: sonnet
reason: B gives a newcomer a mental model first: a five-step summary, explicit ground rules (sub not email, every success ends in start_session, one Google account per user) and a reading guide for the flowchart, while A puts a denser glossary and a very large diagram ahead of its plain step-by-step explanation.

reason: A orients a newcomer better: it starts with a short numbered summary and the ground rules, describes where state lives before showing the diagram, and tells you how to read the flowchart. author: haiku
reason: A opens with one paragraph covering the whole nightly flow and the two facts that drive the design, then follows it with numbered steps and a failure table, and its terms stay consistent throughout; B has better schemas and rationale but conflates run and attempt, giving each attempt its own run_id while also claiming a retry clears its earlier staging by run_id, so a newcomer would trust it less.

author: haiku
reason: I'd rather be handed B. It opens by saying why the design looks the way it does: there's no write access to the app database, and dashboards must never see a partial night. It then walks through numbered steps and adds a scannable failure table, so a newcomer can follow how the system works more easily than in A's denser topic-by-topic notes, even though A argues the lookback window more rigorously.
